item.title: US, Canada, Mexico extend CPA mobility agreement through 2028
item.description: The AICPA and the National Association of State Boards of Accountancy are among the group of entities reaffirming a smooth path for accounting professionals to practice across North American borders.

item.title: AICPA pushes IRS to ease and expand first‑time abatement rules
item.description: The recommendations include allowing taxpayers to rely on substitute reasonable cause when appropriate, permitting them to reserve the automatic first-time abatement for future use.

item.title: PEEC proposes revised definition of 'attest engagement team'
item.description: The AICPA Professional Ethics Executive Committee seeks comment on a revised definition to gather input on whether the definition appropriately reflects the roles that should be excluded from an attest engagement team. The comment deadline is June 1.

item.title: Private Company Council issues annual report
item.description: The report highlights the activities of the group charged with working with FASB to improve the process of setting accounting standards for private companies.

item.title: Adequate identification relief extended through 2026
item.description: The relief allows taxpayers to use alternative methods to make adequate identification of digital asset units that are sold, disposed of, or transferred during the relief period.

item.title: IRS provides guidance on business interest limitation elections
item.description: The guidance in Rev. Proc. 2026-17 is provided in response to H.R. 1’s amendments to Secs. 163(j) and 168(k).

item.title: AICPA seeks clarity on revamped paid family leave credit rules
item.description: The request came in an AICPA letter to Treasury and the IRS seeking guidance on how employers should implement changes to the paid family leave credit.

item.title: Audit report card: More internal audit teams suffered cuts in 2025
item.description: The percentage of internal audit leaders reporting staff and budget reductions in 2025 rivaled numbers during the global financial crisis nearly two decades ago. Strategic alignment was linked to sufficient funding for the function, an annual report showed.

item.title: How listening is shaping ‘incredible’ year for AICPA Chair Lexy Kessler
item.description: Kessler has shared plenty of perspective with members and students around the globe, and the perspective she has gained from them in return has highlighted her year of service.

item.title: IRS watchdog cites resource limits, duplication in partnership audits
item.description: The Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration assessed a soft-letter initiative and the IRS’s examinations of 82 major U.S. partnerships.

item.title: IESBA to assess need for standards on alternative practice structures
item.description: The International Ethics Standards Board for Accountants will examine whether new standards are needed to address ethical considerations related to the prevalence of private-equity investment in the accounting profession — a topic already being addressed by the AICPA Professional Ethics Executive Committee.

item.title: PCAOB seeks comment on strategic priorities
item.description: The PCAOB requested input on its strategic priorities, seeking the answers to seven questions in particular as it develops a new strategic plan.

item.title: SEC accepting Professional Accounting Fellow applications
item.description: The SEC’s Office of the Chief Accountant is accepting applications for positions that will begin this summer. The application deadline is April 22.

item.title: Americans’ financial optimism edges higher, but worries remain
item.description: As National Financial Literacy Month begins, an AICPA-commissioned survey highlights why many consumers need to refocus their financial decision-making.

item.title: IRS tapped Inflation Reduction Act funds to cover 2025 filing season, watchdog says
item.description: TIGTA found the IRS spent $4.8 billion in Inflation Reduction Act funds, which were intended to supplement its annual appropriation, on labor and IT to keep the 2025 tax season on track.
